items.prose: Geothermal heat bleeding down from the emergency diesel exhaust trench raised permafrost temperatures above 2°C. Subterranean methane hydrate crystals dissociated explosively, blowing an eighty-five-centimeter heave through the unreinforced floor slab and filling the gallery with pure methane.

Pressurized sub-permafrost groundwater fed the growth of an internal massive ice core (pingo) directly beneath Seed Vault Annex B. The expanding ice dome pushed the sixty-centimeter reinforced foundation slab four feet upward, snapping structural tie-beams.

Thawing of ground ice wedges along the northern slope triggered a massive retrogressive mud slump. Three thousand tons of liquefied permafrost silt flowed downhill, shearing the main insulated liquid nitrogen fill casing and exposing the portal to surface air.

An unfrozen, highly pressurized groundwater pocket (talik) beneath the hundred-meter permafrost layer breached an exploratory core hole. Sub-zero mineralized brine and dissolved methane erupted into Level 6 at forty bar, coating cryo-tanks in frozen salt rime.

Overpressurized methane bubbling through saturated permafrost clay created a cold mud volcano inside the air intake canyon. A ten-meter cone of liquid blue clay and gravel plugged the emergency air filtration intake louvers.

Warming of an ancient, uncompacted interglacial peat layer beneath Stairwell 2 triggered intense methanogenic bacterial activity. Methane gas seeped through masonry expansion joints, reaching a 9% explosive concentration that detonated when an emergency relay clicked.

Rapid temperature cycling between winter surface cold (-45°C) and bunker internal exhaust (+15°C) created extreme thermal contraction stresses in massive ground ice wedges. A four-meter ice wedge fractured with a sound like a naval cannon, cleaving the tunnel shotcrete.
